images.filename: Eglwys Gallgo Sant - St Gallgo Church, Llanallgo - geograph.org.uk - 1191572.jpg
images.caption:
Eglwys Gallgo Sant/St Gallgo Church, Llanallgo, near to Llanallgo, Isle of Anglesey/Sir Ynys Mon, Great Britain.
Gallo, who founded this church early in the 6thC, was the son of Caw, a Pictish king, and brother of St Gildas and St Eugrad. Like many other old churches in Anglesey it underwent much restoration in Victorian time. It also became famous in the wake of the Royal Charter disaster of 1859 when 140 of the victims were buried in its churchyard. Charles Dickens visited the area and wrote about the disaster. During his visit Dickens stayed at the rectory with the vicar, the Rev. Stephen Roose Hughes

images.filename: A memorial to a victim of the Royal Charter Sinking - geograph.org.uk - 1191402.jpg
images.caption: A memorial to a victim of the Royal Charter Sinking Manus Maurice Boyle. a 26 year old miner was lost when the Royal Charter was wrecked off Moelfre in Oct. 1859. Unlike the 149 buried at Llanallgo, Boyle was one of over 300 whose bodies were never recovered. This monument was erected in his memory in 2004 by the Fay family of Hazelton, Pennsylvania, USA.

images.caption: Mynwent St Gallgo Cemetery This cemetery contains the remains of victims of ship wrecks, most notably, those of the Royal Charter sinking of 1859, as well as those of local seafarers and farmers and their families. Coxswain Dic Evans is also buried here.
